=== Enshrined Deities ===
;Comprehensive divine name
* Ōmi Iwai Ōkami

;East Hall
* Hachidai Ryūō Shrine
** Toyotama-hiko-no-kami, sea deity (maternal grandfather of Emperor Jinmu)
** {{ill|Hikoimasu no Ōkimi|ja|彦坐王|ko|히코이마스노미코|zh|彥坐王|qid=Q11487910}} (third son of Emperor Kaika)
* Shōrei Tennō Shrine
** {{ill|Emperor Tenji|Q314802|qid=Q314802}} (Amenome Oshi Hirakiwake no Sumeramikoto)
** {{ill|Emperor Kōbun|Q357242|qid=Q357242|lt=Prince Ōtomo}} (Emperor Kōbun)
** Iga no Yakatoko-hime (birth mother of Prince Ōtomo)

;West Hall
* Tenjō Shōrai Shrine
** Heavenly and earthly deities
* Ōmi Ryūō Shrine
** Ōmi Ryūō deity
* Fukutoku Shrine
** The Seven Lucky Gods of Iwai
* Ujigami Shrine
** Satabiko no Kami

;Inner Shrine
* Goryōden Shrine
** Iwai Ōkami
** Hachidai Ryūō deity

=== History ===
The date of the shrine’s founding is unknown. According to shrine tradition, Haruta no Muraji, the first provincial governor (kuni no miyatsuko) of the Ōmi Province government established at Seta, buried his ancestor from four generations earlier, {{ill|Hikoimasu no Ōkimi|ja|彦坐王|ko|히코이마스노미코|zh|彥坐王|qid=Q11487910}}, at {{ill|Chausuyama Kofun (Ōtsu)|Q27926911|qid=Q27926911|lt=Mount Chausu}}, and enshrined the mountain behind it, Mount Goryōden, as a {{ill|Sacred mountains|Q1595289|qid=Q1595289}}. This is said to be the origin of the shrine.<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese|url=http://www.shiga-jinjacho.jp/ycBBS/Board.cgi/02_jinja_db/db/ycDB_02jinja-pc-detail.html?mode:view=1&view:oid=67|title=Shrine Introduction|accessdate=2019-07-21|publisher=Shiga Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines}}</ref> After the {{ill|Jinshin War|Q2378252|qid=Q2378252}}, the shrine outwardly enshrined the {{ill|Eight Great Dragon Kings|Q11390736|qid=Q11390736}}, but secretly venerated {{ill|Emperor Tenji|Q314802|qid=Q314802}}, {{ill|Emperor Kōbun|Q357242|qid=Q357242|lt=Prince Ōtomo}}, and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Iga no Uneme Yakako}}.{{Sfn|“Kadokawa Dictionary of Japanese Place Names” Editorial Committee|1979|p=765}}

=== Cultural Properties ===
;Important Cultural Properties
* Wooden seated statue of Amenome Oshi Hirakiwake no Mikoto – Heian period
* Wooden seated statue of Iga no Uneme Yakako-hime – Heian period
* Wooden seated statue of Emperor Kōbun – Heian period
* Wooden seated statue of Hikoimasu no Ō – Kamakura period

;Shiga Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties
* Main hall of Iwai Shrine – Built in {{ill|Bun'ei|Q1010103|qid=Q1010103}} 3 ({{ill|1266|Q5517|qid=Q5517}}), as confirmed by a copy of a ridge tag made in {{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}} 3 ({{ill|1692|Q7685|qid=Q7685}}).{{sfn|Ōtsu City Museum of History|2004|p=26}} It is a three-bay nagare-zukuri structure with {{ill|cypress bark roof|Q90373477|qid=Q90373477}} (cypress bark roofing).{{sfn|Ōtsu City Museum of History|2004|p=26}}

=== Access ===
* 5-minute walk from “{{ill|Nishiki Station|Q7040593|qid=Q7040593|lt=Nishiki}}” on the Keihan Ishiyama–Sakamoto Line
* 9-minute walk from “{{ill|Zeze Station|Q1042692|qid=Q1042692|lt=Zeze}}” on the Tōkaidō Main Line (JR Biwako Line)
* 3-minute walk from “Nishi-no-shō (in front of Ōtsu Prince Hotel)” bus stop on Keihan Bus or Ōmi Railway (bus)
